meiji_transition.summary: Nara Prefecture was set up in 1871, absorbed into Sakai Prefecture in 1876 and with it into Osaka-fu in 1881, then re-established in 1887.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Nara = Yamato Province; in Meiji it briefly vanished into Osaka-fu and was 'restored' only after years of petitioning by local people.

history_timeline.title: Heijō-kyō
history_timeline.summary: The capital moved to Heijō-kyō in 710 and the Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji was consecrated in 752 — the height of the ritsuryō state; Hōryū-ji is the world's oldest surviving group of wooden buildings.

history_timeline.title: Rebuilding Tōdai-ji
history_timeline.summary: After Taira no Shigehira burned Nara in 1180, Chōgen led the rebuilding of Tōdai-ji, and Unkei and Kaikei completed the Kongō Rikishi guardians in 1203.

history_timeline.title: The Southern Court at Yoshino
history_timeline.summary: In 1336 Emperor Go-Daigo fled to Yoshino and founded the Southern Court, beginning over fifty years of rival courts; Kōfuku-ji ruled Nara as governor of Yamato.

history_timeline.title: Warlords of Yamato
history_timeline.summary: Kōfuku-ji long served as Yamato's governor; in 1567 fighting between Matsunaga Hisahide and the Miyoshi Triumvirate burned Tōdai-ji's Great Buddha Hall, and in 1577 Hisahide took his own life at Shigisan Castle.

history_timeline.title: Province of temples
history_timeline.summary: The Kōriyama Domain and the Nara magistrate shared rule; Nara-machi thrived on ink, bleached cloth and Nara-zuke pickles, and Nara's deer were protected.

history_timeline.title: Restoration and heritage
history_timeline.summary: Nara Prefecture was re-established in 1887; Hōryū-ji became World Heritage in 1993 and the monuments of ancient Nara in 1998.

dialect.name: Nara dialect
dialect.features: A Kansai dialect with '-haru' and '-yaru' honorifics; yet around Totsukawa in the south a Tokyo-type accent survives — very rare in Kinki.

phrases.meaning: pray to the gods and Buddhas (said to children)

guide.opening: When I lived in Heijō-kyō, the Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji had only just opened its eyes — the most glorious moment of the ritsuryō state. Would you hear the Great Buddha's story?

regional_meme.title: Nothing good to eat in Nara?
regional_meme.text: 'Nara ni umai mono nashi' — one remark by the writer Shiga Naoya has haunted Nara for a century.

regional_meme.title: More deer than people
regional_meme.text: The deer of Nara Park bow for crackers — and butt you if you don't hand them over.

hero_persona.name: Prince Shōtoku
hero_persona.title: The sage of Asuka
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Prince Umayado, known as Shōtoku Taishi. 'Harmony is to be valued' — the first article of the Seventeen-Article Constitution still lives in Japanese hearts.
hero_persona.tone_prompt: serene and wise, gentle and dignified, speaks of Buddhism and government; legends such as hearing ten people at once should be noted as legends

ramen.toppings: Heaps of spicy stir-fried napa cabbage, garlic chives, pork
ramen.highlight: Spicy cabbage ramen that began at street stalls — Nara's late-night soul food

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: unfiltered, undiluted and lightly fizzy; Nara's Shōryaku-ji is considered the birthplace of refined sake
